To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

soluble ST2 (sST2) is highly increased in follicular fluid compared to plasma levels and is expressed and secreted by granulosa cells. sST2 levels in follicular fluid are increased in larger follicles. sT2 levels in follicles associated with good quality embryos are higher than in those associated with poor quality embryos.
soluble ST2 is highly expressed in human follicles and luteinised human granulosa cells and that higher levels of soluble ST2 are found in follicular fluid associated with good quality embryos.
sST2 is present in human follicles and is secreted by granulosa cells, but cannot be used to identify good quality embryos.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of the soluble ST2 receptor in human follicular fluid.
the role of IL-33/ST2 in human follicles and its potential use as a biomarker of oocyte/embryo quality and ART success.
the role of sST2 in the FF and how it relates to embryo quality, and whether it can be used as an indicator of successful IVF outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sST2 is expressed and secreted by luteinised cells, and that the level of sST2 is associated with oocyte and embryo quality but not ART outcome.
the expression and release of soluble ST2 in follicular fluid is not a reliable marker for oocyte and embryo competence, nor can it be used as a predictor of IVF success.
sST2 levels in FF are higher than in plasma and are associated with oocyte and embryo quality but are not predictive of cycle outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sST2 is highly expressed in the FF, is increased in larger follicles, and may be produced by the luteinised human granulosa cells. sST2 levels in FF may reflect oocyte quality and are higher in successful ICSI cycles.
ST2 is expressed by human luteinized granulosa cells, and that sST2 levels in FF may reflect oocyte competence.
sST2 is a novel biomarker of follicular function and is a potential predictor of oocyte quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sST2 is a soluble cytokine present in FF, and that luteinised human granulosa cells express and se crete this protein.
sST2 is a soluble protein that is highly increased in human follicular fluid, and is secreted by granulosa cells.
sST2 is highly expressed and secreted into the FF of follicles.
